chapterTitle: Chapter 16: Environmental Chemistry & Modern Analytical Techniques
title: Chapter 16: Environmental Chemistry & Modern Analytical Techniques
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: In the atmosphere, the ozone layer that shields the Earth from harmful solar ultraviolet-B radiation (290-320 nm) is located in which atmospheric sphere?
questions.explanation: The stratospheric ozone shield absorbs destructive UV-C and UV-B radiation via the Chapman photolytic cycle: O₃ + hν → O₂ + O.

questions.question: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs / Freons) cause catalytic destruction of stratospheric ozone because ultraviolet radiation photolyzes them to release reactive:
questions.explanation: CF₂Cl₂ + hν → •CF₂Cl + Cl•; each chlorine radical can destroy up to 100,000 ozone molecules via catalytic chain propagation: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂; ClO• + O → Cl• + O₂.

questions.question: Photochemical smog (Los Angeles smog) is an oxidizing smog formed on sunny days by photochemical reactions between:

options.A: Nitrogen oxides (NO_x), unburned volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and sunlight, producing ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN)
options.B: SO₂ and coal smoke in cold damp air

questions.explanation: Automobile exhaust releases NO and hydrocarbons; solar UV splits NO₂ into NO + O, which creates secondary oxidants: ground-level O₃, aldehydes, and eye-irritating PAN.

questions.question: Normal unpolluted rainwater is slightly acidic (pH ~5.6) due to dissolved atmospheric CO₂ forming carbonic acid. Acid rain is defined when rainfall pH falls below:
questions.explanation: Rainwater with pH < 5.6 is classified as acid rain, caused primarily by atmospheric sulfuric acid (from SO₂) and nitric acid (from NO_x).

questions.question: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a vital water quality index that measures:

options.A: The amount of dissolved oxygen consumed by aerobic microorganisms to biologically decompose organic matter in a water sample over 5 days at 20°C
options.B: The total volume of dissolved air in water

questions.explanation: BOD₅ tests oxygen consumption by aerobic microbes. Clean unpolluted water has BOD < 1-2 ppm; heavily polluted sewage water has BOD > 100-400 ppm.

questions.question: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) measures the total organic content in wastewater by oxidizing it chemically using which boiling acidic reagent?
questions.explanation: Boiling with acidified standard K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidizes both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic pollutants, with COD always higher than BOD.

questions.question: Eutrophication of lakes and rivers is caused by excessive runoff of which plant nutrients, leading to algal blooms and eventual aquatic dead zones?

options.A: Phosphates and Nitrates (from agricultural fertilizers and detergents)

questions.explanation: Excess phosphate and nitrate trigger dense blooms of algae; decaying algae consume dissolved oxygen, suffocating fish.

questions.question: Minamata disease, a severe neurological toxic syndrome first discovered in Japan, is caused by bioaccumulation of:
questions.explanation: Industrial methylmercury discharges accumulate in fish, attacking the central nervous system, brain, and motor control.

questions.question: Itai-itai disease ('it hurts-it hurts') is a painful bone-softening and renal failure condition caused by chronic poisoning from:
questions.explanation: Cadmium replaces calcium in human bones, causing severe osteomalacia, multiple fractures, and irreversible kidney damage.

questions.question: In drinking water purification plants, Alum [K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O] is added during the coagulation/flocculation step to:

options.A: Neutralize negative charges on suspended colloidal clay particles, forming a gelatinous Al(OH)₃ floc that traps and settles impurities

questions.explanation: Al³⁺ ions hydrolyze to form sticky Al(OH)₃ gelatinous flocs that sweep down finely suspended silt and microorganisms during sedimentation.

questions.question: The primary disadvantage of chlorinating municipal drinking water containing residual humic organic matter is the formation of carcinogenic byproducts called:
questions.explanation: Chlorine reacts with natural organic matter to produce trihalomethanes (THMs), which are suspected human carcinogens.

questions.question: Which principle of 'Green Chemistry' emphasizes that synthetic methods should be designed to maximize the incorporation of all raw materials into the final product?
questions.explanation: Atom Economy = (Molecular weight of desired product / Molecular weight of all reactants) × 100%; high atom economy minimizes chemical waste.

questions.question: Infrared (IR) Spectroscopy is primarily used by organic chemists to identify:

options.A: Functional groups based on characteristic vibrational stretching and bending frequencies

questions.explanation: Molecules absorb infrared radiation at frequencies resonant with specific bond vibrations (stretching and bending), diagnostic of functional groups.

questions.question: In an Infrared (IR) spectrum, a broad, strong absorption band appearing in the region 3200 - 3600 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of:

options.A: Hydrogen-bonded O-H stretching vibration (alcohols and phenols)

questions.explanation: The O-H bond involved in intermolecular hydrogen bonding gives a broad, intense peak at 3200-3600 cm⁻¹.

questions.question: A sharp, very intense absorption band appearing at 1680 - 1750 cm⁻¹ in an IR spectrum is the diagnostic fingerprint of which functional group?

options.A: Carbonyl group (C=O stretch of aldehydes, ketones, esters, and acids)

questions.explanation: The polar C=O double bond has a large dipole change during vibration, producing a sharp, prominent absorption peak between 1680 and 1750 cm⁻¹.

questions.question: In an IR spectrum, the region below 1500 cm⁻¹ (600 - 1400 cm⁻¹) containing complex overlapping skeletal bending vibrations unique to a specific molecule is called the:
questions.explanation: The fingerprint region is unique to each individual organic compound, just as a human fingerprint identifies a specific person.

questions.question: According to the Beer-Lambert Law in Ultraviolet-Visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, the absorbance (A) of a solution is given by:
questions.explanation: Absorbance A = εcl, where ε is the molar absorptivity (extinction coefficient), c is concentration in mol/L, and l is cuvette path length in cm.

questions.question: In UV-Visible spectroscopy, a covalently bonded unsaturated group that absorbs electromagnetic radiation in the UV or visible region is called a:
questions.explanation: Chromophores ('color carriers') are functional groups with π electrons undergoing π→π* or n→π* transitions in the 200-800 nm range.

questions.question: A functional group containing lone pairs (such as -OH, -NH₂, -OR) that does not absorb UV light on its own but shifts the absorption of a chromophore to longer wavelength is called an:
questions.explanation: Auxochromes attach to chromophores and extend conjugation via lone pair delocalization, red-shifting the absorption maximum (bathochromic shift).

questions.question: A shift of an absorption band toward longer wavelength (lower energy) is known as a:
questions.explanation: Bathochromic (red) shift moves λ_max to longer wavelengths; hypsochromic (blue) shift moves λ_max to shorter wavelengths.

questions.question: In Proton Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (¹H-NMR) spectroscopy, what reference compound is added as an internal standard and assigned a chemical shift (δ) of 0.0 ppm?
questions.explanation: TMS is chemically inert, volatile (b.p. 27°C), soluble in organic solvents, and gives a sharp single resonance peak at higher field than almost all organic protons.

questions.question: In ¹H-NMR spectroscopy, the splitting of NMR signals into multiplets due to spin-spin coupling with adjacent non-equivalent protons follows the:
questions.explanation: A proton with n equivalent neighboring protons splits into a multiplet containing (n + 1) peaks (e.g., 2 neighbors split a signal into a triplet: 2+1=3).

questions.question: In Mass Spectrometry, the peak corresponding to the intact, unfragmented ionized molecule produced by loss of one electron (M•⁺) is called the:
questions.explanation: The molecular ion peak (M•⁺) gives the exact molecular mass (m/z value) of the compound.

questions.question: The most intense (tallest) peak in a mass spectrum, arbitrarily assigned an abundance of 100%, is termed the:
questions.explanation: The base peak represents the most stable and abundantly formed ionic fragment in the fragmentation pathway (normalized to 100%).

questions.question: In chromatography (paper or thin-layer chromatography, TLC), the Retention Factor (R_f) value is calculated as:

options.A: Distance traveled by the solute spot / Distance traveled by the solvent front
options.B: Distance of solvent / Distance of solute

questions.explanation: R_f is a dimensionless ratio between 0 and 1: R_f = (Distance traveled by substance) / (Distance traveled by solvent front).

questions.question: Which greenhouse gas has the largest contribution to the human-induced greenhouse effect and global warming due to the vast volume emitted by fossil fuel combustion?
questions.explanation: While methane is more potent per molecule, CO₂ is responsible for >65% of global radiative forcing due to hundreds of billions of tons emitted globally.

questions.question: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and Gas Chromatography (GC) differ primarily in that:

options.A: GC uses an inert carrier gas (He or N₂) as mobile phase for volatile compounds, whereas HPLC uses liquid mobile phase under high pressure for non-volatile/thermolabile compounds
options.C: GC does not use a column

questions.explanation: GC requires samples to be vaporized into carrier gas without thermal decomposition; HPLC pumps liquid solvents through fine particulate columns for heat-sensitive solutes.

questions.question: The catalytic converter installed in modern automobile exhaust systems uses platinum, palladium, and rhodium to convert harmful emissions into:

options.A: CO, NO_x, and hydrocarbons into harmless CO₂, N₂, and H₂O

questions.explanation: Three-way catalytic converters oxidize toxic CO and unburned hydrocarbons to CO₂ and H₂O, while reducing NO_x to harmless nitrogen gas (N₂).

questions.question: What is the primary toxic effect of lead (Pb²⁺) poisoning on human health, especially in young children?

options.A: Inhibits enzymes for heme synthesis (causing anemia) and damages developing central nervous system, lowering IQ

questions.explanation: Lead inhibits aminolevulinic acid dehydratase, causing anemia, encephalopathy, and permanent neurodevelopmental cognitive deficits.

questions.question: In ¹H-NMR spectroscopy, how many distinct resonance signals are observed for pure Ethanol (CH₃-CH₂-OH)?

options.A: Three signals (ratio 3 : 2 : 1 corresponding to -CH₃, -CH₂-, and -OH protons)

questions.explanation: Ethanol possesses three chemically non-equivalent sets of hydrogen atoms: 3 methyl protons, 2 methylene protons, and 1 hydroxyl proton.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds will show only ONE sharp singlet in its ¹H-NMR spectrum?
questions.explanation: In acetone, all six protons belong to two identical, symmetrical methyl groups attached to the same carbonyl carbon, producing a single singlet (δ ~2.1 ppm).

questions.question: The international treaty signed in 1987 to phase out production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances (CFCs and halons) is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol successfully regulated and phased out CFCs, stabilizing and beginning the recovery of the stratospheric ozone layer.

questions.question: What is the m/z value of the molecular ion peak for Benzene (C₆H₆) in a mass spectrum?
questions.explanation: Molecular weight of C₆H₆ = (6 × 12.011) + (6 × 1.008) = 78 g/mol; hence the molecular ion peak appears at m/z = 78.

questions.question: Arsenicosis (arsenic poisoning) from drinking tubewell water contaminated with natural inorganic arsenic (As³⁺) causes characteristic:

options.A: Blackfoot disease and hyperpigmentation/keratosis of palms and soles

questions.explanation: Chronic arsenic poisoning damages peripheral blood vessels (Blackfoot gangrene) and causes characteristic raindrop skin pigmentation.

questions.question: In Green Chemistry, supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO₂) is widely used as a 'green solvent' to replace toxic chlorinated solvents in:

options.A: Decaffeination of coffee beans and dry cleaning of textiles

questions.explanation: Supercritical CO₂ is non-toxic, non-flammable, renewable, and evaporates completely leaving zero harmful chemical residue.
